claims.claim: Skill discovery resolves roots from cwd/config/plugin/extra-root inputs and bundled-skill settings.

evidence.point: skill_roots_for_config derives roots from config, cwd, plugins, and extra roots before loading.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Root availability and filesystem authority vary by environment and config.
claims.final_wording: Skill discovery resolves configured roots before metadata becomes available to the turn.

claims.claim: Skill snapshots are cached by cwd or skill-relevant configuration and contain metadata/errors for later turn use.

evidence.point: snapshot_for_config and snapshot_for_cwd return HostSkillsSnapshot values and use separate cache maps.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Cache keys and invalidation behavior are implementation details that can change.
claims.final_wording: Skill snapshots are reusable metadata/error projections keyed by the relevant cwd or configuration.

claims.claim: Discovery parses and validates SKILL.md metadata without automatically injecting the full skill body.

evidence.point: load_skills_from_roots delegates to root loading; parser structures require frontmatter name/description and enforce size limits.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: A later extension/context path can read the body as a separate operation.
claims.final_wording: Discovery validates skill metadata; body injection is a later, explicit read path.

claims.claim: The app-server skills watcher clears skill caches after relevant skill changes.

evidence.point: Watcher event loop clears SkillsService cache on skill changes.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Watcher availability and event delivery depend on the owning app-server/environment.
claims.final_wording: When the app-server watcher observes a relevant change, it invalidates skill snapshots for later reload.

claims.claim: Skill catalogs are assembled through source-specific providers that preserve resource authority.

evidence.point: SkillProvider exposes list/read/search and requires resources to remain within their authority.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Provider implementations can differ in capabilities and enforcement details.
claims.final_wording: Catalog and resource operations remain routed through the provider that owns the skill authority.

claims.claim: TUI/app-server skills/list is a client management/read path distinct from the model-facing skills.list tool.

evidence.point: Catalog processor implements skills/list and skills/config/write request paths.
TUI exposes /skills and calls the app-server skills/list path.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Surface names and exact wire fields are versioned protocol details.
claims.final_wording: Client-facing skills/list management is separate from the model's namespaced skills.list tool.

claims.claim: Structured UserInput::Skill selects an enabled skill by explicit path and suppresses duplicate/disabled selections.

evidence.point: collect_explicit_skill_mentions resolves structured UserInput::Skill by enabled path.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Selection still depends on the catalog snapshot supplied to the function.
claims.final_wording: Explicit structured skill inputs resolve enabled catalog entries by resource identity.

claims.claim: Text skill mentions resolve exact resource paths first and plain names only when enabled and unambiguous.

evidence.point: Text inputs are scanned for tool mentions and selected only when path/name rules succeed.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Mention syntax and ambiguity rules are implementation-specific.
claims.final_wording: Text mentions select skills through path identity or an enabled unambiguous name match.

claims.claim: Explicit skill body reads use the skill's filesystem/provider authority and turn read failures into warnings.

evidence.point: build_skill_injections reads through a filesystem authority and turns errors into warnings.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: A successful read makes content available for context; it does not grant command execution authority.
claims.final_wording: A selected skill body is read through its authority and either becomes an injection fragment or produces a warning.

claims.claim: Available skill metadata is rendered under a token/character budget and can be truncated or omitted with warnings.

evidence.point: build_available_skills selects allowed skills, applies budget, and reports omitted/truncated descriptions.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Budget behavior does not guarantee every skill description is fully visible to the model.
claims.final_wording: Skill metadata is model-visible only through the active context budget and may be shortened or omitted.

claims.claim: The skills extension contributes catalog/world-state context and stores turn-local selection/read state.

evidence.point: Turn contributor reads selected main prompts and stores SkillsTurnState.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: The extension can be disabled or omit sources based on configuration/environment.
claims.final_wording: When enabled, the extension contributes skill context and keeps selection state scoped to the thread/turn.

claims.claim: Implicit invocation detection recognizes a bounded set of interpreter/script forms and matching SKILL.md reads, but does not execute them.

evidence.point: The detector checks supported runners/extensions and parsed SKILL.md reads.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Other command syntaxes may execute successfully without being attributed by this detector.
claims.final_wording: Implicit detection is attribution logic for recognized paths, not a process-spawn mechanism.

claims.claim: Implicit skill attribution is deduplicated per turn and emits contributor, metric, and analytics records.

evidence.point: Implicit invocation uses a scope/path/name seen key, notifies contributors, increments a metric, and tracks InvocationType::Implicit.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Telemetry delivery is not equivalent to a durable execution trace.
claims.final_wording: Implicit attribution is emitted once per skill/path/name key per turn and recorded in observability systems.

claims.claim: The model-facing skills.list tool returns bounded opaque handles for the supported orchestrator authority.

evidence.point: ListTool returns bounded package/name/description/main-resource handles.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: The current tool implementation supports only the orchestrator authority; host skills use other context paths.
claims.final_wording: skills.list exposes bounded opaque handles for the authority it supports, not ambient host paths.

claims.claim: The model-facing skills.read tool rechecks handles/authority and reads through the same provider before returning structured output.

evidence.point: ReadTool validates handles, checks enabled authority/package, reads provider resource, and returns external JSON.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Provider errors and unavailable packages return model-visible errors rather than content.
claims.final_wording: skills.read treats list-returned handles as opaque, revalidates them, and routes the read through the owning provider.

claims.claim: The provider trait separates list/read/search and forbids converting an authority-owned resource into an ambient local path.

evidence.point: Provider boundary is explicit in SkillReadRequest and provider-owned resource routing.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: The trait is a contract; each provider still needs implementation/tests to establish its concrete behavior.
claims.final_wording: Skill resources remain routed through the provider/authority that owns their handles.

claims.claim: A skill script command is executed by the shell/unified-exec runtime, while implicit detection only attributes the command to a skill.

evidence.point: The detector recognizes script paths but returns SkillMetadata rather than spawning a process.
UnifiedExecRuntime owns process execution and the ToolRuntime path.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: A skill may recommend other executors or remote tools; this claim covers the inspected local unified-exec path.
claims.final_wording: Skill attribution and process execution are separate calls; skill metadata does not itself spawn a CLI process.

claims.claim: Local command execution applies approval and sandbox controls independently of skill instructions.

evidence.point: The runtime exposes sandbox permissions and approval keys before execution.
Skill tests exercise approval and authority-specific filesystem reads.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: Remote MCP/connectors have different process/credential boundaries and are not covered by the local sandbox formula.
claims.final_wording: A skill recommendation still enters the executor's applicable approval and sandbox boundary before local execution.

claims.claim: Skill injection and implicit attribution emit observability records, while normal tool results remain correlated to the originating call.

evidence.point: Implicit invocation path tracks analytics and increments codex.skill.injected.
Explicit injection records SkillInvocation analytics after a successful body read.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: These metrics/analytics are not a complete durable process trace.
claims.final_wording: Skill observability records supplement, but do not replace, the normal correlated tool result path.

claims.claim: Disabled, oversized, missing, or failed skills are filtered, truncated/omitted, or surfaced as warnings rather than silently treated as successful injection.

evidence.point: Renderer creates warnings when descriptions or entries exceed the configured budget.
Extension tests cover selected skill list/body injection and failure behavior.

claims.counterevidence_or_limits: A warning is not proof that a downstream model followed or saw every warning.
claims.final_wording: Skill failure and budget paths remain explicit through filtering, warnings, and omission/truncation outcomes.
